title: R(12,12) ≥ 1661: a red/blue colouring of the edges of K_1660 with no monochromatic K_12
abstract: The diagonal Ramsey number R(12,12) is at least 1661: there is a simple graph on 1660 vertices such that neither the graph nor its complement contains a clique on 12 vertices, that is, a red/blue colouring of the edges of K_1660 with no monochromatic K_12. The graph is built from the Mathon–Shearer (11,11)-colouring M(797) on 1596 vertices by deleting a set of 21 vertices, which contains two antipodal pairs of M(797), and adding 85 core vertices, each of which copies a deleted vertex or has a single colour towards the remaining 1575 vertices. The proof is a clone-projection argument with an antipodal rule. It uses that M(797) has no monochromatic K_11 (proved in Lean here, following r1212-1642), that antipodal vertices of M(797) have opposite colours towards every other vertex, and finite checks on the 85 core vertices that the Lean kernel evaluates with decide +kernel. The construction and the proof are described in the preprint hexagon:2611.00248. This repository is a port of the formalization in https://github.com/YueMa0/r1212-1661 (Lean 4.32.1) to Lean 4.35.0 and the module system.
